It was based in the city of [[Donetsk]] until 2014, when the [[War in Donbas (2014–2022)|War in Donbas]] forced the club to relocate. It moved from the [[Donbas Arena]] to Lviv (2014–2016) and then to [[Kharkiv]] (2017–2020), whilst having its headquarters and training facilities in [[Kyiv]].[https://web.archive.org/web/20190901201647/https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/dcunited/still-in-exile-shakhtar-donetsk-picks-new-home/2017/01/30/6e1f075c-e6f4-11e6-903d-9b11ed7d8d2a_story.html Still in exile, Shakhtar Donetsk picks new home], [[The Washington Post]] (30 January 2017) In May 2020, Shakhtar started to play home matches at [[Olympic Stadium (Kyiv)|NSC Olimpiyskyi]].[https://www.ua-football.com/ua/ukrainian/high/1590586848-shahtar-provede-zalishok-sezonu-na-olimpiyskomu.html Shakhtar will spend the rest of the season at the Olimpiyskiy] Since the beginning of the 2023–24 season, Shakhtar has played home matches once again at [[Arena Lviv]].{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28440553 |title=Shakhtar Donetsk move training and games over Ukraine conflict |publisher=BBC Sport |date=23 July 2014 |access-date=28 August 2014}} Shakhtar became the first Ukrainian club to win a UEFA competition after Ukrainian independence when the team won the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]] in [[2008–09 UEFA Cup|2009]], the last year before the competition was revamped as the Europa League, by defeating [[Werder Bremen]] [[2009 UEFA Cup final|2-1]]. Shakhtar is one of two Ukrainian clubs who have won a major UEFA competition, the other being [[FC Dynamo Kyiv|Dynamo Kyiv]]. It is one of Ukraine's most popular clubs, is particularly favoured in the eastern [[Donbas]] region.[http://www.interfax.co.uk/ukraine-news/poll-40-of-ukrainians-consider-themselves-football-supporters-most-against-idea-of-cis-league/ Poll: 40% of Ukrainians consider themselves football supporters, most against idea of CIS league], [[Interfax-Ukraine]] (27 August 2013){{cite web|url=https://www.footballbusinessinside.com/how-shakhtar-donetsk-plans-its-future-in-kiev/|title=How Shakhtar Donetsk plans its Future in Kiev|website=Football Business Inside|date=28 October 2021}} The club draws its history from the very start of the Soviet football league competitions and is one of the oldest clubs in Ukraine. The club was a member of the Soviet [[Voluntary Sports Societies of the Soviet Union|Voluntary Sports Society]] of Shakhtyor, having connections with [[FC Shakhter Karagandy|Karaganda]] ([[Kazakhstan]]) and [[FC Shakhtyor Soligorsk|Soligorsk]] ([[Belarus]]) among others. In the late Soviet period, Shakhtar was considered a mid-table club of the [[Soviet Top League]] and won the [[Soviet Cup]] two years in a row, in 1961 and 1962."}}
